segments.text: Silver ETFs versus physical silver: The tax difference is everything.
segments.narration: Silver ETFs versus physical silver: The tax difference is everything.

Both physical silver and silver ETFs like SLV get taxed at the same federal long-term capital gains rate of up to 28 percent, because the IRS classifies both as collectibles. That is the headline most investors miss. The real differences live in short-term treatment, state sales tax, dealer reporting thresholds, and what happens when you actually sell.
When you sell SLV shares held longer than one year, your gain hits a maximum federal rate of 28 percent, the same ceiling that applies to a tube of Silver Eagles in your safe.

A buyer in the 32 percent bracket owes $480. A buyer in the 12 percent bracket owes $180. The lesson is simple: silver is a position, not a trade. Hold past the one-year mark or expect to give back a third of your profit.

Physical silver has zero phantom basis adjustments. Your basis is what you paid, period. Physical sales above certain thresholds trigger a 1099-B. Dealer 1099-B reporting is triggered on physical silver sales of 1,000 troy ounces or more of .999 fine bars in a single transaction (Source: JM Bullion).

Run the numbers before you buy, not after. Here is the formula we use with customers comparing a $10,000 physical purchase to a $10,000 SLV position, both held two years, both gaining 40 percent. But the physical buyer holds metal that does not depend on a custodian, a brokerage, or a trust agreement.

Check your state's department of revenue website before you buy. The 1099-B threshold and the 28 percent federal rate do not, but state tax can move 8 percent of your purchase price in or out of your pocket. Three errors show up over and over on customer questions.

If you are buying for a one to three year horizon and live in a sales-tax state, SLV likely produces better after-tax returns. If you are building a five to twenty year position and want metal outside the financial system, physical wins despite the 28 percent rate and any local sales tax.
